newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares ends lower on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares ends lower on profit taking.

text.p: Profit taking almost across the board on the Jakarta stock exhange saw the bourse's index close lower on Friday, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index fell 3.44 points, or 0.55 percent, to close at 624.46 points after touching an intra-day low of 623.16 points.
Decliners led losers by 69 to 33, with 59 steady counters. Total volume reached 443.9 million shares on a turnover valued at 1.4 trillion rupiah.
Brokers and analysts said the market was likely to be mixed on Monday with follow-through profit taking expected to combine with ongoing weak regional markets due to a weaker Dow Jones.
Some counters were likely to rise and draw market attention by buying their own shares to improve the firm's price, known as year-end window dressing, they said.
But volume-wise, total transactions would be small as some investors were checking out for holiday season, they added.
"As usual, many companies are doing year-end window dressing, so its possible the index could be maintained at its current level," Sastra Karta, fund management director of PT Bhakti Investama said.
Overall market sentiment on Friday was dampened by weak regional markets after it was hit by the sharp fall in the Dow Jones overnight, brokers said.
Banking stocks including Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) and a few blue-chips such as Telkom and Indosat were the target of profit-takers, brokers said.
BNI was the most active stock with 9.9 million shares traded, falling 25 rupiah to 1,300 rupiah, while Bank International Indonesia fell 50 rupiah to 2,175 rupiah on 3.3 million shares.
Heavyweight Telkom fell 25 rupiah to 3,950 rupiah on 3.7 million shares changing hands, while Indosat fell 25 rupiah to 6,350 rupiah on 1.1 million shares.
Despite weak market sentiment, a few issues made significant gains including tin miner Tambang Timah, brokers said.
World-scale tin miner Tambang Timah rose 5.73 percent, or 225 rupiah to 4,150 rupiah on a volume of 1.3 million shares following on fresh buying, brokers said.

"It was boosted by the recent news saying that Tambang Timah had shown interest in joining in the development of the world's biggest gold find in Busang in Kalimantan," a broker with foreign firm said.
